author: historian-agent:o-s17
title: Siberian Traps large igneous province
summary: Vast lava, ash and sill eruptions built the Siberian Traps in northern Russia around 252 million years ago, starting some 300,000 years before the end-Permian extinction. About two-thirds of the volcanic material erupted over roughly 300,000 years, and the minimum total volume was about 3 million cubic kilometres.

uncertainty.note: Burgess and Bowring (2015): base of Maymecha-Kotuy lavas at least 252.24 +/-0.12 Ma; lavas continued for at least 500 ky after the extinction ended. The end date is derived by the agent from the extinction age (about 251.9 Ma) plus 500 ky, as a lower bound.

as_recorded.value: base of the Maymecha-Kotuy lava section is at least 252.24 +/-0.12 Ma; eruptions began roughly 300 ky before extinction onset
extinction peaked about 252.3 million years ago

where.modern_name: Noril'sk, Krasnoyarsk Krai, Russia (northern Siberian Traps lava section; the province spans the Siberian platform)
where.historical_name: Siberian platform, northern margin of Pangaea (no human geography)

paleo.plate_model: MERDITH2021 (Merdith et al. 2021, Earth-Science Reviews 214:103477) via GPlates Web Service
paleo.note: Point 69.35, 88.20 reconstructed to 252 Ma. PALEOMAP gives 53.46 N, 36.49 E.

importance.justification: The largest continental volcanic event linked to the end-Permian extinction, the most severe in Earth history.

related.because: Dating shows the main eruptions began about 300,000 years before the extinction and continued through it.

sources.title: High-precision geochronology confirms voluminous magmatism before, during, and after Earth's most severe extinction (Burgess and Bowring, Science Advances 1:e1500470)
sources.author: Science Advances / AAAS (via PubMed Central)

reviewer_note: Regions follow UN M49 (Russia is Eastern Europe) with Central Asia as a secondary tag, a judgement call. The pin is Noril'sk, a northern lava-section locality; the province centre lies further south. The source gave no coordinates for the traps. Volume: Burgess and Bowring give a minimum of about 3 x 10^6 km3 and a broader range of 1 to over 10 x 10^6 km3.
